title: Deal intake form and required artifacts (non-standard enterprise deals)
author: Irene Choi
content:
## Purpose
This page defines the **Deal Intake Form** and the required artifacts for the **end-to-end process for getting a non-standard enterprise deal approved and signed at Redwood Inference**.

The intake form is the shared checklist used by Sales, Deal Desk, Legal, Security, and Finance to ensure all gates are completed before signature.

## What qualifies as a non-standard enterprise deal
A deal is considered non-standard if it requires any approvals outside the normal AE + Sales Manager flow. Common triggers:
- Discount exception beyond standard bands
- Customer paper or edits to Redwood templates
- DPA required or changes requested
- Security questionnaire or custom audit language
- Net terms beyond Net 30, PO constraints, or non-standard invoicing cadence
- SLA changes or special service credits

## Where the form lives
- The Deal Intake Form is created as a single record linked from the CRM deal record.
- The form must include links/attachments to the latest versions of all customer documents.

## Deal Intake Form fields (required)
### A) Deal summary
- Customer legal entity name
- Customer domain
- Deal owner (AE) and Solutions Engineer
- Products in scope: Hosted API / Dedicated / Private
- Deployment region(s) and data residency constraints
- Target signature date and target go-live date

### B) Commercials
- Term length (months)
- ARR/ACV estimate
- Proposed pricing and effective discount
- Usage assumptions (if Hosted API)
- Ramp schedule (if any)

### C) Contracting
- Redwood paper vs customer paper
- Documents required: MSA, Order Form, DPA, SLA addendum, security exhibit
- Key clauses flagged by customer (liability, indemnity, audit, breach notification)

### D) Security & compliance
- Security questionnaire required (yes/no)
- SOC 2 requested (yes/no)
- Audit rights requested (yes/no)
- On-prem / air-gapped requirements (yes/no)

### E) Billing
- Payment terms requested
- PO required (yes/no)
- Bill-to entity and address
- Invoicing cadence
- Tax/VAT requirements or exemptions

## Required artifacts checklist
Attach/link these before requesting final approvals:
- Customer paper (editable format preferred)
- Proposed Order Form (latest draft)
- Pricing calculation output and discount band
- Security questionnaire (if applicable)
- Customer procurement requirements (PO policy, vendor onboarding)

## Gate sequencing (recommended)
This is the recommended order for the end-to-end process:
1) Intake form completed
2) Pricing approvals (Discount Approval Matrix)
3) Security review (if needed)
4) Legal redlines + Approved to Send
5) Billing setup approval
6) Send for signature + store executed PDFs

## Definition of done (deal signed)
A non-standard enterprise deal is considered approved and signed when:
- Approvals are recorded (pricing, legal, security if applicable, billing)
- Contract is executed and stored
- CRM record includes final term, SKU set, and billing contacts

Use the linked pages for each gate; this intake page is the orchestration layer.
